notes:
*** THE DOCUMENTED FAILURE MODE DID NOT REPRODUCE — IT IS WORSE THAN 'MASKED' ***
create_custom_field_dataset_v2's guidance (and this capability's own guidance) warns that mapping a project to a second dataset when a sibling dataset already claims it 'fails with the upstream message relayed verbatim (e.g. Projects already linked to a different dataset for this custom field..., invalid project mapping, Dataset id is invalid)'. That did not happen. Attempt 1 mapped 31320 to PR-2005 (already owned by 31319) and got a clean 200/success:true — and 31319's own mapping was silently deleted as a side effect, with no error, no field in either response indicating a conflict occurred, and no way for a caller to learn about it short of independently re-reading the sibling dataset. This is not 'the error is masked' — there is no error at all. The one-project-one-dataset-per-field rule is enforced by silent last-writer-wins reassignment, not by rejection. Any caller who maps a project believing they are only adding it to their own dataset can unknowingly detach it from whatever dataset previously held it, with a 200 telling them everything is fine.

*** PUT vs PATCH: THIS ONE IS GENUINELY ADDITIVE (unlike edit_test_run) ***
Attempt 2 sent link_projects:[379339429] with 31320 already holding PR-2005 from attempt 1, and did NOT send PR-2005 in the same call. Result: linked_project_count went 1 -> 2, both projects present. Sending a link_projects list does NOT replace the dataset's project list — it adds to it, exactly as the parameter-level guidance says ('Integer project ids to ADD'). This is the opposite of edit_test_run.test_case_ids, which claims 'additive' in its docs but is actually a full replace. Here the docs and the behavior agree: link_projects/unlink_projects are true deltas against the existing list, not a replacement of it. Confirmed the inverse too in attempt 3 (unlink_projects:[379335744] alone removed exactly that one project, leaving PR-2011 untouched) and attempt 4 (relinking 31319 to PR-2005 did not steal PR-2011 back off of 31320 — the exclusive-ownership reassignment in attempt 1 was specifically about the SAME project moving between datasets, not a wholesale replace of any dataset's list).

*** link_to_future_projects: reflected immediately, plus one undeclared side-channel ***
Setting link_to_future_projects:true on attempt 2 was echoed back verbatim in the same call's response, and drove the undeclared future_projects_applicable field from 0 to 1 in lockstep (attempt 3 flipped both back to false/0 together). Whether it actually auto-links a newly created project was not tested further (out of scope, and doing so would have required creating another throwaway project) but the flag is real, is honored, and now correctly sits at false on both 31320 and 31319 after cleanup.

*** DRIFT CLUSTER — CONFIRMED ON THIS CAPABILITY TOO ***
- data.options: declared array, always an object {data,info} in practice, identical to get_custom_field_dataset's confirmed drift (this endpoint returns the freshly re-read dataset, so it inherits that read's shape).
- datasetProjects: present and undeclared on every call, an exact duplicate of the declared linked_projects — same second-copy pattern flagged on the parent create probe.
- Everything must be verified by reading back: this capability's OWN write response is trustworthy for the dataset it targets (the re-read `data` block is accurate, unlike create_custom_field_dataset's write response, which returns options:{} regardless of content) — but it says NOTHING about side effects on other datasets. The PR-2005 theft from 31319 was invisible in attempt 1's response and only surfaced by independently re-reading 31319.

CLEANUP: dataset 31320 ends this probe linked only to 379339429/PR-2011 (linked_project_count 1, link_to_future_projects false) — the intended legitimate mapping. Sibling dataset 31319 ends restored to its original state, linked only to 379335744/PR-2005 (linked_project_count 1) — the incidental detachment caused by the deliberate collision test (attempt 1) was corrected by attempt 4. Both states were verified live by get_custom_field_dataset reads after the corrective calls, not inferred from write responses. No 500s, no status:0/hang — the v2-tier outage flagged as a risk for this capability did not manifest; all 4 writes and both verification reads returned promptly with 200.
